html:
SMTO-SKL-0109 — The file didn't arrive complete or unchanged

GUID: 0ef99567-a39b-55b7-b796-b7996709965c
Slug: microsoft365-transfer-integrity-failed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • When copying a file to or from OneDrive or SharePoint, the file's size or contents didn't match what was expected. SMTO stopped instead of using a damaged or changed file.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were downloading, make sure nobody is editing the file in OneDrive or SharePoint, then ask the Agent to download it again. The file may have changed while it was being copied.
  2. If you were uploading, attach or create the file again in this conversation, then ask the Agent to upload that new copy. The saved copy in SMTO no longer matches what was recorded, so a fresh copy is needed.

What success looks like

  • The Agent reports the transfer as complete and the file opens normally.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't upload a file that keeps failing this check; it may be damaged.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • File integrity check failed: a OneDrive/SharePoint download's byte count differed from the item's metadata size, or an upload source artifact's size or SHA-256 no longer matches its registered record.

What this means

  • Download size differs from expected metadata, or selected source bytes fail the registered size/SHA-256 check. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Download size differs from expected metadata, or selected source bytes fail the registered size/SHA-256 check.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare actual bytes with the retained size/hash for the exact revision.

How to fix it

  • For downloads, re-read the item metadata (file_info) and download again; the item may have changed during the transfer. For uploads, the source artifact's bytes differ from its recorded size_bytes/sha256; regenerate or re-register the artifact in the conversation, then upload the new artifact reference.
  • Fetch fresh exact-file metadata for downloads or restore the correct registered source bytes before another transfer.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended file passes integrity checks before publication or upload.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
